findings.evidence: EfronStein.lean:133 `theorem efronStein {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] ...`; nothing in the proof depends on `Fin`.
findings.fix: State it for `{ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ}` using `Measure.pi fun _ : ι => gaussianReal 0 1`.
findings.issue: `variance_le_sum_integral_fderiv_sq_pi` is restricted to `Fin n → ℝ`. The proof only uses `efronStein`, `integral_integral_update_pi` and `contDiff_update`, and all three work for any finite index type.

findings.evidence: The proof uses `hC` only to build `hint` via `integrable_of_abs_le`, and the target measure is exactly `Measure.pi μ` (`map_update_prod_pi`).
findings.fix: Replace `hh : Measurable h` and `hC` with `hh : Integrable h (Measure.pi μ)`. Obtain `hint` from `MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp`, and use `hh.aestronglyMeasurable` for the change of variables.
findings.issue: `integral_integral_update_pi` requires `h` to be measurable and bounded (`|h x| ≤ C`). Integrability under `Measure.pi μ` is enough: `map_update_prod_pi` makes the update map measure-preserving, so the composed function is integrable on the product.

findings.evidence: mathlib Gaussian/Multivariate.lean:126 `lemma stdGaussian_map ... (f : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] F) : (stdGaussian E).map f = stdGaussian F`; :135 `map_pi_eq_stdGaussian`.
findings.fix: Derive it from `stdGaussian_map` together with `map_pi_eq_stdGaussian` (or `IsGaussian.ext`), or state the general fact (the product of standard Gaussians is invariant under any linear isometry equivalence) and specialize. Otherwise make the lemma private.
findings.issue: `measurePreserving_orthogonal_gaussianReal` re-proves, by hand-computed characteristic functions, one 2×2 case of Gaussian rotation invariance. Mathlib already proves invariance under every linear isometry (`stdGaussian_map`) and identifies the product of standard Gaussians with `stdGaussian` (`map_pi_eq_stdGaussian`).

findings.evidence: mathlib Gaussian/Basic.lean:155 `lemma IsGaussian.charFunDual_eq (L : StrongDual ℝ E) : charFunDual μ L = exp (μ[L] * I - Var[L; μ] / 2)`; Basic.lean:60 `instance isGaussian_gaussianReal`.
findings.fix: Remove it and use `IsGaussian.charFunDual_eq` (or `IsGaussian.charFunDual_eq_of_integral_eq_zero`). If a closed form is wanted, state it for general `gaussianReal m v`.
findings.issue: The public `charFunDual_gaussianReal_zero_one` is the mean-0, variance-1 case of Mathlib's `IsGaussian.charFunDual_eq`, which already applies to `gaussianReal m v` through the `isGaussian_gaussianReal` instance.

summary: The tensorized Poincaré inequality is stated only for `Fin n`, but its sole tool (`efronStein`) works over any finite index type; the resampling lemma asks for boundedness where integrability is enough. Two public Gaussian helper lemmas re-prove narrow cases of rotation-invariance and characteristic-function results Mathlib already has.
